headline: OPEC fails to agree on a price, every member sets its own
text: OPEC oil ministers met in Caracas from 17 to 20 December and could not agree a common price. Each of the 13 members may now charge what the market will bear: asking prices run from 24 to 30 dollars a barrel, and Libyan crude is reported near 35 from New Year. In June the cartel's ceiling was 23.50. Whoever fills a tank will feel it.

headline: Soviet troops storm into Kabul and kill Afghanistan's president
text: Soviet forces began taking key points in Kabul on 25 December, and on the 27th they stormed the palace of President Hafizullah Amin, who was killed. Moscow has put Babrak Karmal in his place; some 30,000 Soviet troops were sent for the operation. How the West will answer is not yet clear.

headline: Fifty-odd Americans still held in Tehran, the UN calls for their release
text: Students seized the US embassy in Tehran on 4 November, and more than fifty Americans are still prisoners, six weeks later. The UN Security Council called for their release on 4 December. The students demand that the Shah, the exiled ruler, be handed back, and that frozen Iranian money be released.

headline: America's war on inflation: prices up 11.3 percent this year
text: Prices rose 11.3 percent in 1979. The new head of the Federal Reserve, Paul Volcker, announced on 6 October that the central bank would stop steering interest rates directly and control the supply of money instead, which lets rates jump. The key rate was about 11 percent this year. Borrowing has become expensive for everyone.

headline: Gold passes 500 dollars as the world looks for safety
text: Gold ended December above 500 dollars an ounce, more than twice what it cost a year ago. With oil prices jumping, inflation high, hostages in Tehran and troops in Afghanistan, buyers want something that holds its value. Silver ended the year at 34.45 dollars, up from under 10 in summer, as two Texas brothers, the Hunts, buy it by the million ounces.

headline: Star Trek comes to the cinema
text: Star Trek: The Motion Picture had its premiere on 6 December at the Smithsonian Institution in Washington. A darker note on 3 December: eleven fans died in a stampede at a concert by The Who in Cincinnati.
